# Independent central-tetrahedron audit and one-full-row support payment

## 1. the contributor source audit

Full independent audit **PASS** for Sections 1–5 of
`candidate 3ed628996d1cbb09`.

The diagonal coordinates and the quadrilateral centroid formula are correct. In the AC triangulation, the ABC and ACD relative areas are (y+z)/S and (x+w)/S; the opposite coefficients express the diagonal intersection on BD. Thus the section centroid equals (A+B+C+D−e)/3. The displayed barycentric coordinates follow.

The captured-volume expression was independently checked against the exact simplex CDF for heights (−1/x,−1/y,1/z,1/w). The condition 1−3lambda_1≥0 equals c/[(y+z)(y+w)S]≥0, with c as printed. The polynomial identity (5) is exact; its denominator is positive, and its numerator is strictly positive when c≥0 because bA>0. Repeated positive heights require no limit because the rational diagonal parametrization and determinant formula remain valid.

The one-vertex formula is an exact tetrahedral determinant, including edge intercepts equal to one. For the complement of a vertex cap the difference is exactly 1−27 lambda_j lambda_k(1−lambda_j−lambda_k), which is nonnegative by three-term AM–GM. These cases cover all non-quadrilateral proper incidences, including cuts through vertices and edges.

For Section 3, a minimizing through-source normal exists by compactness of the unit sphere and continuity of cap volume. Its normal derivative is the stated first section moment, including a cut through vertices: writing points as b+w+sn reduces a normal perturbation to moving the threshold to −epsilon v·w/(1+epsilon v·n). At relative-interior points of the proper section the fiber interval contains zero strictly. Its boundary has zero relative area, and all threshold shifts are bounded by a constant times |epsilon| on the bounded projection. Dominated convergence therefore gives the derivative. Vanishing for every tangent normal direction forces the actual section centroid to be b. The upper vertex-cap construction with intercepts 3b_j is valid, including intercept one. This verifies the exact ordinary-depth formula throughout the stated central barycentric region.

The two-coordinate face of D_d is exactly the stated l_p ball. Raising the two row-product inequalities to p=d/(d−1), dropping the factors bounded by one, and using geometric-mean superadditivity proves necessity. The explicit matrix with two cross entries one and equal theta/(1−theta) allocations in each remaining column proves sufficiency, including zero endpoint coordinates.

The arbitrary-probability two-coordinate capacity argument uses only the covering events U≤t or V≤1−t. The infimum definition gives the CDF upper bounds even with atoms, and minimization of the displayed convex power sum gives (a^p+b^p)^(1−d). Zero capacities and d=1 are separately valid. No three-coordinate probability claim is being made.

The exact checker `supporting computation verify_central_tetrahedral_cap_audit_two_sided.py` passes 1,979 checks, including symbolic reconstruction of the printed cap polynomial identity, the actual section centroid, boundary vertex incidences, and the two-coordinate-face construction for dimensions 2 through 9. The general proofs, not those finite dimensions, establish the all-d statement.

## 2. Weakly captured vertices in the central tetrahedral lemma

The root source's inequality (8) also holds for a vertex lying on the proper section plane, provided every section-centroid coordinate is at most 1/3.

To see this directly, a proper tetrahedral section through a vertex r is a triangle having r as one vertex. Its other two vertices lie in the opposite facet, so its centroid has lambda_r=1/3. This remains true if the plane contains an edge: the section is a triangle with both edge endpoints as vertices. There is at least one strictly captured vertex s. The root theorem gives

    F≥27 product_(j≠s)lambda_j.

Since lambda_s≤lambda_r=1/3 and all section-centroid coordinates are positive,

    product_(j≠r)lambda_j
       =product_(j≠s)lambda_j ·lambda_s/lambda_r
       ≤product_(j≠s)lambda_j.

Thus the desired inequality holds also when r is only weakly captured. No limiting argument is needed.

## 3. Support payment with exactly one full regular row and all three other rows present

Consider d=3 and a weighted capacity maximizer as in the audited section-centroid source. Assume it has exactly one full proper regular differentiable row r. Assume every other row is nonzero with exactly one zero, and their three missing columns are distinct. After the permitted matching permutation put each missing entry on its diagonal. The full row is x, its minimizing cap has fraction F, threshold t, and section centroid b. Normalize the positive column multipliers to sum one; scale all objective weights by the same factor. The audited equations give

    lambda_j=b_j>0,       b_j≤1/3,
    c_i=3 GM((b_j)_(j≠i))=:c_i^0  for i≠r,
    c_r=F^(1/3),
    H(X)=1,
    (1−x_r)b_r=(1−t)/3.                               (17)

Because b_r≤1/3, the last identity implies x_r≤t. The full-row label is therefore a weakly captured vertex of its actual minimizing tetrahedral cap. The central cap theorem, with the preceding boundary extension, yields

    F≥27 product_(j≠r)b_j,
    c_r≥c_r^0.                                        (18)

Define the actual zero-diagonal column-stochastic matrix

    Y_ij=(1/3−b_i)/b_j   for i≠j,       Y_ii=0.          (19)

Its entries are nonnegative, and in each column the numerator sum equals b_j. Every row satisfies

    c_i^0 GM(Y_i,off)=1−3b_i,

including zero rows when b_i=1/3. Thus

    Σ_i c_i GM(Y_i,off)
       =1+(c_r/c_r^0−1)(1−3b_r)
       ≥1=H(X).                                      (20)

This pays the weighted support comparison by an explicit matrix in D_3. It does not claim that the original multipliers are dual-feasible for the full row; indeed (18) has the opposite direction from that unnecessary assertion. If b_r=1/3, row r of Y is zero and (20) holds with equality regardless of the size of c_r/c_r^0. Boundary cuts are therefore harmless.

The hypotheses matter. Rows sharing a missing column can be merged, but this leaves an identically zero row; that resulting stratum is not automatically covered by Section 3, since its weight need not equal c_i^0. The separately proved at-most-two-nonzero-row theorem handles one full row plus only one surviving zero row. One full row plus two surviving zero rows, and maxima with more than one full row, remain separate statuses unless another proof covers them.

This is a scoped support-payment theorem under actual maximizing necessary conditions, not the general stochastic theorem and not OC.
